relevant_findings.topic: Exterior trim repaint substrate state is the primary estimation driver
relevant_findings.finding: Unlike NC where substrate state is singular (factory-primed or bare), repaint exterior trim presents four distinct substrate states: SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT, SS_EXT_CHALKING, SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT, SS_EXT_PEELING. Each state drives a fundamentally different prep pathway, primer decision, and labor multiplier. The substrate state + substrate condition (DSD-equivalent SC_SOUND through SC_SEVERE_DETERIORATION) together form a two-dimensional matrix that is the dominant cost driver for trim repaint estimation.

relevant_findings.topic: DSD-equivalent condition assessment drives prep labor multiplier
relevant_findings.finding: MPI Degree of Surface Degradation (DSD) ratings translated to SC_* enum values drive prep labor multipliers: SC_SOUND (DSD-0/1) = 1.0-1.25x baseline, SC_SLIGHT_DETERIORATION (DSD-1) = 1.15x midpoint, SC_MODERATE_DETERIORATION (DSD-2) = 1.375x midpoint, SC_SEVERE_DETERIORATION (DSD-3) = 1.75x midpoint. These multipliers apply to ALL prep tasks and stack multiplicatively with height multipliers. Formula: Effective Rate = Baseline Rate / (DM x HM) where DM = deterioration multiplier and HM = height multiplier.

relevant_findings.topic: Multiple trim components measured in LF with distinct PS keys
relevant_findings.finding: Exterior trim is not a single surface. This spec covers 8 distinct trim components, each with its own PaintScope key: fascia (PS_EXT_EDGE_LF.FASCIA), rake (PS_EXT_EDGE_LF.TRIM_RAKE), frieze (PS_EXT_EDGE_LF.TRIM_FRIEZE), corner boards (PS_EXT_EDGE_LF.TRIM_CORNER), band board (PS_EXT_EDGE_LF.TRIM_BAND), window casing (PS_EXT_EDGE_LF.TRIM_WINDOW_CASING), door casing (PS_EXT_EDGE_LF.TRIM_DOOR_CASING), and sill (PS_EXT_EDGE_LF.SILL). All measured in LF per PCA P10 one-foot rule: trim <12 inches wide = 1 SF per 1 LF.
relevant_findings.source: PaintScope_Exterior_Key_Catalog.md Section Exterior Edge Keys; Exterior_Trim_Systems_Doctrine.md

relevant_findings.topic: Feather-edge sanding is mandatory at all scraped areas
relevant_findings.finding: Every area where existing paint is scraped must be feather-edge sanded to create a smooth transition between bare substrate and remaining sound paint. Without feather sanding, the old paint edge creates a visible ridge ('mapping') that telegraphs through topcoats. This is a non-negotiable quality standard at all tiers (QT3-QT5). Production rate for feather sanding on trim: 30-50 LF/hr depending on profile complexity.

relevant_findings.topic: Lead-safe RRP gate for pre-1978 buildings
relevant_findings.finding: Pre-1978 coatings may contain lead. EPA Lead-Safe RRP practices are required before any Class II or Class III paint removal (scraping, sanding, heat gun). RRP is a GATE CONDITION, not a separate spec. When triggered, all prep tasks receive an RRP modifier for containment, HEPA vacuum, wet scraping, and lead-safe disposal. Must evaluate existing coating before disturbing. Trim is a HIGH RISK surface for lead paint because historically trim received oil-based lead paint more frequently than field surfaces.

relevant_findings.topic: Three substrate material types require different primers
relevant_findings.finding: Exterior trim may be traditional wood, cellular PVC (AZEK, VERSATEX), or engineered wood (LP SmartSide). Each material requires a different primer system when bare areas are exposed during prep. Wood: acrylic stain-blocking or alkyd stain-blocker for tannin-rich species. PVC: bonding primer formulated for non-porous substrates. Engineered wood: mandatory edge sealing on all field-cut edges (warranty requirement) + acrylic primer. Substrate material is a MODIFIER (not configuration dimension) because it affects primer selection only, not the overall workflow.

relevant_findings.topic: Height modifier is trim-specific, not FAC_EXT_ACCESS
relevant_findings.finding: Trim height modifiers differ from siding access modifiers because trim is found at ALL elevations — fascia and rake are at roofline, casings span ground to second story, corner boards run full height. Trim-specific height tiers from doctrine: ground level (0-8 ft) = 1.00x, first elevation (8-13 ft) = 1.30x, second elevation (13-17 ft) = 1.60x, high elevation (17-19 ft) = 1.90x, extreme elevation (19+ ft) = 2.20x. Use FAC_TRRP_HEIGHT, not FAC_EXT_ACCESS.

Built-up trim profiles (multi-piece crown assemblies, elaborate window surrounds with cap/sill/pilaster, dentil frieze boards) add 30-60% to production time. A simple flat 1x4 corner board is baseline; a 3-piece crown with dentil returns takes 1.60x baseline. Complexity modifier is applied per component, not per project — one building may have simple corner boards but elaborate window surrounds.

relevant_findings.topic: Caulking is integral to trim repaint workflow
relevant_findings.finding: Trim repaint includes caulk assessment and replacement at all trim-to-adjacent-surface joints. The 'Think Like a Water Drop' protocol from doctrine: SEAL corner joints, trim-to-siding gaps, door casing joints, window perimeters. NEVER CAULK weep holes, bottom overlap of siding, metal-to-wood flashing, bottoms of overlapping trim. PVC requires solvent-based polymer or polyurethane caulk (NEVER silicone). Caulk replacement rate for repaint: 50-100 LF/hr (slower than NC due to old caulk removal step).

relevant_findings.topic: Brush is primary application method for trim
relevant_findings.finding: Exterior trim is predominantly brush-applied. Spray is used only when sufficient continuous trim volume justifies masking overhead (e.g., full-house trim repaint with all siding already masked). Brush production rate for trim: 40 LF/hr (exterior trim average, ground level, simple profile). Spray system rate 'including masking' at 200 SF/hr from doctrine is a SYSTEM rate — individual spray task rate is higher (100-150 LF/hr for the spray pass itself); masking is a separate task.

relevant_findings.topic: Trim is a fine-finish substrate — QT3-QT5 range
relevant_findings.finding: Unlike siding (QT2-QT4), trim IS a fine-finish substrate. Trim sheens are satin, semi-gloss, or high-gloss. QT3 (satin) is standard, QT4 (semi-gloss) is premium, QT5 (gloss) is superior. QT2 is inappropriate for trim — trim is a detail surface where economy prep is not acceptable. At QT5, trim receives additional interstage sanding, two-coat primer, and ultra-smooth brush technique.

relevant_findings.topic: Rot repair is outside painting scope
relevant_findings.finding: When condition assessment reveals wood rot in trim components, the rot repair itself is carpentry/contractor scope — not painting scope. The painting spec must FLAG rot locations and EXCLUDE those areas from LF totals until repair is complete. After carpentry repair, the repaired section enters the spec as SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD (new wood spliced in) and receives full prep/prime treatment.

Cellular PVC trim (AZEK, VERSATEX) has high thermal expansion coefficient. Dark colors (LRV <55) on PVC can cause thermal distortion — warping, buckling, joint opening. When PVC trim is identified as the substrate material, coatings must have LRV >=55 OR be solar-reflective technology (e.g., Sherwin-Williams VinylSafe, Benjamin Moore Regal Select Exterior). This is a material-specific gate condition.

Repaint trim cannot be estimated without inspecting existing surface condition. Assessment includes: visual DSD rating per component, adhesion testing (ASTM D3359 cross-hatch), moisture content (pin meter), existing coating identification (solvent test for alkyd vs latex), rot probe at vulnerable joints (sill corners, fascia-to-rake, bottom of corner boards). Assessment is a REQUIRED fixed-time task. Time: 1.0-2.0 hrs depending on building size and component count.

relevant_findings.topic: Chalking on trim requires dedicated remediation
relevant_findings.finding: Chalking on exterior trim (UV-degraded resin binder releasing pigment) requires the same chalk remediation protocol as siding: hand-rub test, cleaning hierarchy from rinse to mechanical sand to pressure wash, 24-48 hour drying, re-test. If chalk cannot be fully removed, chalk-binding primer is mandatory. Trim-specific note: pressure washing trim at high elevations requires careful control to avoid water intrusion at joints.

relevant_findings.topic: Spot prime vs full prime decision tree
relevant_findings.finding: Prime coat on trim repaint is conditional on substrate state and bare area percentage. SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT: spot prime bare/thin areas only (no full prime if adhesion passes). SS_EXT_CHALKING: chalk-binding primer on all chalked areas. SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT: spot prime all scraped areas; full prime if >30% bare. SS_EXT_PEELING: full prime required (extensive bare substrate). Primer type also varies by substrate material (wood vs PVC vs engineered).

condition_drivers.name: Substrate State
condition_drivers.impact: Primary driver — determines prep pathway, primer selection, and labor scope. Each state activates/deactivates different prep task sets.
condition_drivers.notes: SS_EXT_WEATHERED excluded from trim (trim is always coated or bare; weathered = bare wood which enters via rot repair). SS_EXT_STAINED_* excluded — stained trim is a separate scope.

condition_drivers.name: Substrate Condition (DSD-equivalent)
condition_drivers.impact: Prep labor multiplier: SC_SOUND = 1.0x, SC_SLIGHT = 1.15x, SC_MODERATE = 1.375x, SC_SEVERE = 1.75x. Multiplier applies to prep tasks only, not coating tasks. SC_SUBSTRATE_DAMAGE (DSD-4) = hard stop — outside painting scope (rot repair required).
condition_drivers.notes: Stacks multiplicatively with height modifier. SC_SUBSTRATE_DAMAGE triggers scope exclusion and rot flag.

condition_drivers.name: Quality Tier
condition_drivers.impact: QT3: baseline prep, 2 finish coats, satin sheen. QT4: thorough prep, interstage sanding, 2 finish coats, semi-gloss. QT5: maximum prep, 2-coat primer, interstage sanding between all coats, 2 finish coats, gloss. Trim IS fine-finish — QT2 excluded.
condition_drivers.notes: QT5 adds interstage sanding, ultra-smooth brush technique, and 2-coat primer. Trim quality is highly visible — economy tiers not appropriate.

condition_drivers.name: Application Method
condition_drivers.impact: Brush is primary for trim (40 LF/hr baseline). Spray conditional on sufficient volume and masking justification (100-150 LF/hr spray pass, but masking is separate task). Application method drives protection zone activation — spray requires siding masking, window masking, door masking.
condition_drivers.notes: Spray on trim only when full-house trim repaint justifies masking overhead. brush_roll not applicable — trim is too narrow for roller on most profiles.

condition_drivers.name: Height
condition_drivers.impact: Applied per component based on working height. Fascia/rake at roofline = high or extreme tier. Casings at ground level = baseline. Corner boards span multiple tiers — use highest applicable tier.
condition_drivers.notes: Uses FAC_TRRP_HEIGHT, not FAC_EXT_ACCESS. Trim-specific height tiers differ from siding access tiers.

condition_drivers.name: Profile Complexity
condition_drivers.impact: Applied per component type. Simple flat board = baseline. Standard routed profile (clamshell, ogee) = 1.15x. Built-up multi-piece assemblies = 1.30x. Elaborate with dentil/returns = 1.60x.
condition_drivers.notes: Uses FAC_TRRP_COMPLEXITY. Per-component, not per-project. One building may have simple corner boards (1.0x) and elaborate window surrounds (1.60x).

condition_drivers.name: Substrate Material
condition_drivers.impact: Affects primer selection only. Wood: acrylic or alkyd stain-blocker. PVC: bonding primer + LRV check. Engineered: edge sealer + acrylic primer. Does not change workflow structure — only which primer product is selected.
condition_drivers.notes: Uses MOD_TRRP_SUBSTRATE_TYPE. PVC triggers LRV gate (>=55 or solar-reflective coating).

condition_drivers.name: Lead-Safe RRP
condition_drivers.impact: Pre-1978 buildings: 1.40x labor premium on ALL prep tasks involving paint disturbance. Adds containment setup/teardown fixed-time tasks. HEPA vacuum, wet scraping, lead-safe disposal.
condition_drivers.notes: Gate condition — triggered by building year. Trim is HIGH RISK for lead paint (historically received oil-based lead paint more frequently than siding).

QT3.prep_level: Standard prep — clean, scrape loose paint, feather-sand scraped areas, spot prime bare areas. Single pass inspection.
QT3.inspection: Visual check for holidays, runs, sags. One pass.
QT3.notes: Baseline for trim repaint. Satin sheen is standard exterior trim.

QT4.prep_level: Thorough prep — all QT3 tasks plus interstage sanding (150-grit) between coats, systematic defect fill, and two-pass inspection.
QT4.coat_system: Conditional prime (state-dependent) + 2 finish coats with interstage sand.
QT4.inspection: Two-pass: first for defects, second for uniformity. Mark and repair.
QT4.notes: Premium trim finish. Semi-gloss accentuates every imperfection — thorough prep mandatory.

QT5.prep_level: Maximum prep — all QT4 tasks plus 2-coat primer system, interstage sanding between every coat (primer and finish), ultra-smooth brush technique with flow additive.
QT5.coat_system: 2-coat primer + 2 finish coats with interstage sand between all 4 coats.
QT5.inspection: Critical inspection at every stage. Near-zero defect tolerance. Raking light inspection for final coat.
QT5.notes: Superior trim finish. Gloss is unforgiving — any brush mark, dust nib, or sag is visible. Reserved for high-end residential and historic restoration.

failure_modes.description: Wood trim rot concentrated at horizontal surfaces (sills, fascia at rake junction, bottom of corner boards) where water pools. Most common repaint failure — painting over rot is cosmetic-only and fails within one season.
failure_modes.prevention: Condition assessment with rot probe at vulnerable joints. Flag and exclude rotted areas. Rot repair = carpentry scope. After repair, new wood enters spec as bare substrate.
failure_modes.impact_on_spec: Rot detection is part of condition assessment task. SC_SUBSTRATE_DAMAGE triggers exclusion. LF totals adjusted after rot repair.

failure_modes.description: PVC requires bonding primer — standard latex does not adhere. Failure presents as peeling sheets within 6-12 months. Also fails when LRV <55 dark colors cause thermal cycling beyond PVC expansion limits.
failure_modes.prevention: Identify PVC during assessment. Use bonding primer. Check LRV before color approval. Solar-reflective coating required for dark colors.
failure_modes.impact_on_spec: Substrate material modifier drives primer selection. LRV gate condition on color approval.

failure_modes.description: Cedar and redwood trim contain water-soluble extractives that bleed through latex coatings as brown/yellow stains. Occurs when bare wood is exposed (scraped areas) and primed with non-blocking primer.
failure_modes.prevention: Alkyd stain-blocking primer mandatory on tannin-rich species when bare wood is exposed. Do not use latex primer on bare cedar/redwood trim.
failure_modes.impact_on_spec: Substrate material modifier (wood sub-type) drives primer selection. TSK_TRRP_SPOT_PRIME and TSK_TRRP_FULL_PRIME must select tannin-blocking primer for cedar/redwood.

failure_modes.description: Failed caulk at trim-to-siding and trim-to-trim joints allows water entry behind paint film, causing peeling, rot, and substrate damage. Most common cause of premature trim coating failure.
failure_modes.prevention: Replace all failed caulk during prep phase. Use sealant compatible with substrate (silicone NEVER on PVC). Test adhesion of new caulk to old substrate.
failure_modes.impact_on_spec: Caulk replacement is integral prep task (TSK_TRRP_CAULK_REPLACE). LF of caulk joints estimated from trim component count and typical joint frequency.

failure_modes.description: LP SmartSide and similar engineered wood products swell irreversibly when field-cut edges are not sealed. The resin-bound wood strand matrix absorbs moisture at unprotected edges. Manifests as raised/swollen edges at cuts, miters, and notches.
failure_modes.prevention: Seal every field-cut edge with manufacturer-specified edge sealer. Inspect cut edges during assessment — existing swelling indicates prior improper installation.
failure_modes.impact_on_spec: Edge sealing is part of substrate material modifier (engineered_wood). Flag existing edge swelling as carpenter scope.

failure_modes.description: Decades of repainting without stripping creates excessive paint buildup. Deep cracks perpendicular to wood grain indicate reduced flexibility and vapor permeance. Common on fascia, window casings, and sills with high sun exposure.
failure_modes.prevention: When cross-grain cracking is present, partial or full strip may be required. This escalates to DSD-3+ prep. Multiple repaints are cumulative — each coat reduces flexibility.
failure_modes.impact_on_spec: Condition assessment detects cross-grain cracking. May trigger SC_SEVERE_DETERIORATION rating even on otherwise sound-looking paint.

notes_for_materials_manager: Primer selection is driven by BOTH substrate state AND substrate material. Create a 2D lookup: state (4 states) x material (wood/PVC/engineered). Example: SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT + wood = acrylic stain-blocker on bare spots; SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT + PVC = bonding primer on bare spots; SS_EXT_CHALKING + any = chalk-binding primer.

Tannin-blocking alkyd primer is mandatory for cedar and redwood trim when bare wood is exposed. This overrides the default acrylic stain-blocker for standard wood species. Create a tannin_risk flag that upgrades primer type.
PVC trim primer must be bonding primer formulated for non-porous plastic surfaces. Standard acrylic and alkyd primers will not adhere to PVC. SYS_PRIMER_BONDING or equivalent.
Engineered wood edge sealer is a separate material from primer — it is a penetrating resin applied to cut ends before any coating. Not the same as spot primer.

Caulk product selection varies by substrate: wood = acrylic latex or polyurethane. PVC = solvent-based polymer or polyurethane (NEVER silicone — silicone prevents future paint adhesion on PVC). Engineered = acrylic latex.
Chalk-binding primer (Loxon Acrylic Conditioner type) for SS_EXT_CHALKING state — low-viscosity, high-penetration resin. Not a standard primer — it is a specialty product.
Finish coat sheen per QT: QT3 = satin, QT4 = semi-gloss, QT5 = gloss. All exterior acrylic latex. QT5 may use flow additive for self-leveling brush finish.
Material waste factor for exterior trim: +15% per PCA P10. Trim has higher waste than field surfaces due to small-area brush application and frequent container changes.
RRP materials (when triggered): 6-mil poly sheeting for containment, HEPA vacuum bags, lead-safe disposal bags, misting bottle for wet scraping. These are consumables, not coating materials.
notes_for_sop_librarian: Module sequence: MOD_TRRP_ASSESS → MOD_TRRP_SETUP → MOD_TRRP_PREP → MOD_TRRP_PRIME → MOD_TRRP_INTERSTAGE (QT4/QT5) → MOD_TRRP_FINISH → MOD_TRRP_CLEANUP. Assessment is ALWAYS first — it determines which subsequent modules and tasks activate.

Condition assessment module (MOD_TRRP_ASSESS) is mandatory and includes: visual DSD rating per component, adhesion testing (ASTM D3359), moisture content testing (pin meter), existing coating ID (solvent test), rot probe at vulnerable joints. Fixed time: 1.0-2.0 hrs.

Prep module (MOD_TRRP_PREP) tasks are conditional on substrate state. SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT activates: wash, light sand, spot prime only. SS_EXT_PEELING activates: wash, heavy scrape, feather-sand, full prime. Build task inclusion rules per state.
Feather-edge sanding task (TSK_TRRP_FEATHER_SAND) is MANDATORY whenever scraping occurs — it is NEVER optional regardless of quality tier. Every scraped edge must be feathered.

Caulking module tasks: assess existing caulk → remove failed caulk → clean joint → apply new caulk. Per 'Think Like a Water Drop' protocol — specify which joints to seal and which to NEVER seal (weep holes, bottom overlaps, flashing).

RRP module (MOD_TRRP_RRP) is a conditional wrapper — when lead_status triggers, it adds containment setup before prep, wet method requirements during prep, HEPA cleanup after prep, and disposal at teardown. These wrap around existing prep tasks, not replace them.

Spray application module (MOD_TRRP_SPRAY_SETUP) is conditional on application_method = spray. Adds masking tasks for siding, windows, doors adjacent to trim. Masking time is a SEPARATE task from spray application — do not combine into system rate.

Interstage module (MOD_TRRP_INTERSTAGE) activates at QT4 (sand between finish coats) and QT5 (sand between all coats including primer). Interstage sand grit: 150-180 for between coats, 220+ for final sand before top coat at QT5.

Height modifier is applied per-component, per-task. A single project has tasks at multiple height tiers — fascia tasks use high/extreme tier while casing tasks use ground tier. Build height as a per-component attribute, not project-level.
Complexity modifier is per-component. Simple flat trim = 1.0x. Standard profile = 1.15x. Built-up = 1.30x. Elaborate = 1.60x. This affects ALL tasks on that component (prep and coating).
notes_for_estimation_engineer: Primary UOM is LF for all trim components. PCA P10 one-foot rule: trim <12 inches wide = 1 SF per 1 LF. All production rates are expressed as LF/hr.

Modifier stacking formula: Effective Rate = Baseline Rate / (Condition_Multiplier x Height_Multiplier x Complexity_Multiplier x RRP_Multiplier). Maximum theoretical stack: SC_SEVERE (1.75) x Extreme Height (2.20) x Elaborate (1.60) x RRP (1.40) = 8.624x. This exceeds the 4.0x flag threshold — flag and recommend T&M for extreme combinations.
Condition multiplier (DSD) applies to PREP tasks only. Height and complexity multipliers apply to ALL tasks. RRP multiplier applies to prep tasks involving paint disturbance only.
Each trim component has its own PS key and can have different height and complexity values. The engine must process each component independently and sum LF-weighted results.

Production rates (QT3 baseline, ground level, simple profile): brush finish coat 40 LF/hr, scrape loose paint (light) 40-60 LF/hr, scrape (moderate) 20-40 LF/hr, scrape (heavy) 10-20 LF/hr, feather-sand 30-50 LF/hr, spot prime brush 60-100 LF/hr, full prime brush 50-80 LF/hr, caulk replace 50-100 LF/hr.

Spray production rates (when application_method = spray): spray finish coat 100-150 LF/hr (spray pass only), masking adjacent surfaces 30-50 LF/hr (separate task). System rate combining spray + masking ≈ 50-75 LF/hr — often slower than brush for small-to-medium trim volumes.

Fixed-time tasks (per project): condition assessment 1.0-2.0 hr, moisture testing 0.5-1.0 hr, lead evaluation 0.5-1.0 hr, RRP containment setup 1.0-2.0 hr per zone, RRP containment teardown 0.5-1.0 hr per zone.
Coat system: conditional prime (state-dependent) + 2 finish coats at QT3/QT4. QT5: 2-coat primer + 2 finish coats = 4 total coating passes with interstage sand between each.

Caulk LF estimation: derive from component count and typical joint frequency. Fascia: 1 joint per 8-12 LF (board joints). Window casing: perimeter of each opening. Corner boards: 2 joints per run height (siding-side). Band board: joints at corners and splices.
SC_SUBSTRATE_DAMAGE (DSD-4) = HARD STOP. Engine must exclude affected components from estimation and flag for carpentry scope. Remaining components proceed normally.
Environmental conditions (wind, dew point, sun, temp) are EXCLUDED from estimation modifiers — they are SOP/process concerns per established exterior spec convention.
production_rate_summary: All rates are QT3 baseline, ground level (0-8 ft), simple flat profile. Apply height, complexity, condition, and RRP multipliers as applicable.
Brush finish coat: 40 LF/hr — primary application method for trim repaint.
Spray finish coat (spray pass only): 100-150 LF/hr — excludes masking time.
Masking adjacent surfaces for spray: 30-50 LF/hr — separate task, not combined with spray rate.
Scrape loose paint (light, SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT at SC_SLIGHT): 40-60 LF/hr.
Scrape loose paint (moderate, SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT at SC_MODERATE): 20-40 LF/hr.
Scrape loose paint (heavy, SS_EXT_PEELING at SC_SEVERE): 10-20 LF/hr.
Feather-edge sand (all scraped areas): 30-50 LF/hr.
Light sand / scuff (SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT prep): 60-80 LF/hr.
Spot prime brush: 60-100 LF/hr (rate based on affected LF, not total trim LF).
Full prime brush: 50-80 LF/hr.
Full prime spray: 100-150 LF/hr (spray pass only).
Chalk remediation (light): 80-120 LF/hr — rinse + brush + detergent.
Chalk remediation (heavy): 40-60 LF/hr — mechanical sand or controlled pressure wash.
Caulk replace (remove old + clean + apply new): 50-100 LF/hr.
Power wash trim (low pressure 500-1000 PSI): 100-200 LF/hr — careful control at joints to prevent water intrusion.
Condition assessment: 1.0-2.0 hr per project (fixed time).
Moisture testing: 0.5-1.0 hr per project (fixed time).
Lead evaluation: 0.5-1.0 hr per project (fixed time).
RRP containment setup: 1.0-2.0 hr per work zone (fixed time).
RRP containment teardown: 0.5-1.0 hr per work zone (fixed time).
PVC scuff sand (220-grit): 60-80 LF/hr — required when PVC surface is glossy.
Engineered wood edge seal: 40-60 LF/hr — penetrating sealer on cut edges.

zones.notes: Mask siding adjacent to trim during spray application. Paper and tape along trim-siding junction. Not needed for brush application — brush work on trim does not generate overspray onto siding.

zones.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to full_cover when application_method = spray
zones.notes: Mask window glass when painting window casings. Brush: tape at glass edge. Spray: full glass masking with paper/film.

zones.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to full_cover when application_method = spray
zones.notes: Mask door face and glass when painting door casings. Brush: tape at casing-door junction. Spray: full door cover.

zones.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to full_cover when application_method = spray or when scraping generates debris
zones.notes: Landscape and ground surface protection from scraping debris, wash water, and paint drips. Drop cloth at base of work area. Scraping generates paint chips that must be contained (especially with RRP).
Protect roofing material (shingles, flashing) when painting fascia and rake boards. Tape and paper at roofline edge. Minimal — paint drips on asphalt shingles are difficult to remove.

zones.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to full_cover when scraping or spray generates debris
zones.notes: Walkways and patio surfaces below trim work areas. Drop cloth runners. Paint chips from scraping and wash water contain old coating material.
Exterior light fixtures mounted on or adjacent to trim. Bag or tape over fixture. Common on fascia, casing, and corner boards.

protection_zones_analysis.method_escalation: brush < spray (spray adds siding_mask, upgrades window/door to full_cover)
protection_zones_analysis.cross_spec_protection_note: Siding field protection during trim work is conditional on application method. Brush trim work does not require siding masking. Spray trim work requires siding masking along all trim-siding junctions. Siding masking is THIS spec's responsibility when trim is being sprayed — it protects siding FROM trim spray overspray.
protection_zones_analysis.repaint_specific_note: Repaint trim prep (scraping) generates debris that requires ground-level containment. This is distinct from application protection — scraping debris containment is active during prep phase, not just coating phase. RRP adds additional containment requirements for lead-safe debris collection.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Trim terminates at siding field. Typically different color (body vs trim). No wet-edge blending across specs. Protection relationship only — mask siding when spraying trim.
Soffit adjacent to fascia and frieze. Often same color as trim (white/light). Soffit painting is a separate spec but may share finish group.
Foundation below corner boards and band board. Not painted in this scope. Drop cloth at grade.
Window glass adjacent to window casing trim. Glass is protection target — mask when painting casings.
Door face adjacent to door casing trim. May be same or different color. Door painting is a separate spec.
Masonry wall adjacent to trim in brick/stone houses. Not painted in trim scope.

adjacency_analysis.key_finding: Trim surfaces have linear adjacencies with field surfaces (siding, masonry, soffit) and openings (window glass, door faces). All adjacencies are protection relationships — no edge work or wet-edge blending required across specs. Trim is the INNER surface relative to field — trim is painted after siding in typical sequence, requiring siding protection. Caulking at trim-to-siding junction is THIS spec's responsibility.

affected_task_types: all prep tasks involving paint disturbance
affected_conditions.notes: RRP gate condition. Pre-1978 trim is HIGH RISK for lead paint. Triggers containment, wet methods, HEPA, disposal. RRP modifier on all prep tasks. Fixed-time containment setup/teardown tasks added.

excluded_conditions.rationale: Environmental conditions are important to the painting PROCESS but are NOT estimatable. They are unpredictable, change daily, and cannot be set as fixed conditions for an estimate. They belong in SOP procedure notes and job-site decision protocols, not in production rate modifiers.

excluded.reason: Unpredictable. Changes hourly. Cannot set a fixed modifier for estimate.
Varies by time of day, sun angle, and season. Not predictable at bid time.
Weather-dependent. Not predictable at bid time.
Varies by elevation and season. Professional painters 'follow the shade' — this is scheduling, not estimation.

valid_input_states.rationale: Repaint trim covers four existing-coating states. Each state drives a different prep pathway and primer decision. SS_EXT_WEATHERED excluded — trim that has lost all coating is effectively bare wood, which enters scope via rot repair as SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD. SS_EXT_STAINED_* excluded — stained trim is a separate scope. SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD is NC spec domain (unless after rot repair, in which case just the repaired section receives NC-style treatment within this spec).

output_state.rationale: Output state is the new painted finish. Semi-gloss is the most common exterior trim sheen. Actual output varies by quality tier: QT3 = SS_EXT_PAINTED_SATIN, QT4 = SS_EXT_PAINTED_SEMIGLOSS, QT5 = SS_EXT_PAINTED_GLOSS (via controlled_enums.json mapping).

adjacent_state_protection_analysis.rationale: Repaint context: siding may be freshly painted (protect from trim spray overspray — full mask required) or awaiting its own repaint (light mask sufficient for brush drips). Unlike NC, siding is rarely bare — it has existing coating.
Soffit at fascia/frieze junction. If already repainted, light mask. If awaiting repaint, no protection needed — existing coating is acceptable to get minor drips.
Glass is always a protection target regardless of state. Tape at glass edge for brush. Full paper/film mask for spray.

exterior_substrate_states.description: Previously painted trim with coating intact and well-adhered. ASTM D3359 rating 4A-5A.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Power wash to clean (500-1000 PSI, careful at joints). Light sand or liquid sander for adhesion tooth. Spot-prime any bare/thin areas.
exterior_substrate_states.primer_type: Spot prime only — acrylic stain-blocking primer on bare areas. No full prime needed if adhesion test passes.
exterior_substrate_states.notes: Easiest repaint scenario. Existing coating provides sound base. Skip full prime if adhesion test passes. Minimal scraping — isolated bare spots only.

exterior_substrate_states.description: Previously painted trim with chalky but adhered coating surface. UV-degraded resin binder releasing pigment as powder.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Chalk remediation: cleaning hierarchy from rinse to mechanical sand to pressure wash. Hand-rub test to verify removal. 24-48 hour drying. Re-test. Prime with chalk-binding primer if complete removal not achieved.
exterior_substrate_states.primer_type: Chalk-binding primer (Loxon Acrylic Conditioner type). Low-viscosity, high-penetration resin that soaks through chalk residue and locks it to stable substrate.
exterior_substrate_states.notes: Common on south/west-facing fascia and rake with high UV exposure. Trim chalking is often more visible than siding chalking because trim is at eye level and often darker sheen.

exterior_substrate_states.description: Previously painted trim with cracking, checking, alligatoring, or localized peeling. ASTM D3359 rating 2A-3A.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Scrape all loose/flaking paint via carbide hand scrapers. Feather-sand ALL scraped edges (mandatory). Spot prime bare areas. If >30% bare, full prime required.
exterior_substrate_states.primer_type: Acrylic stain-blocking primer on bare areas. If tannin-rich wood exposed: alkyd stain-blocker mandatory. Full prime if >30% of component LF is bare.
exterior_substrate_states.pca_level: PCA P14 Level 2 (Standard) to Level R (Restoration) for DSD-3
exterior_substrate_states.notes: Prep time varies by failure extent and component. Trim profiles make scraping slower than flat siding. Feather-edge sanding is critical on trim due to close-up visibility.

exterior_substrate_states.description: Active peeling paint on trim — widespread adhesion failure. ASTM D3359 rating 0A-1A. Large ribbons/flakes detaching.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Heavy scraping. May require heat gun for heavy buildup (NOT on PVC). Sand to sound substrate. Full prime required on all bare areas.
exterior_substrate_states.primer_type: Full coverage primer. Acrylic stain-blocking for standard softwoods. Alkyd stain-blocker for tannin-rich wood. Bonding primer for PVC. Deep-penetrating oil-alkyd if wood surface is degraded.
exterior_substrate_states.notes: Most labor-intensive prep state. Trim scraping at height (fascia, rake) is extremely slow due to awkward positioning and profile complexity. RRP required if pre-1978 and paint disturbance > 2 SF on building exterior. Lead-safe containment mandatory if triggered.

exterior_height_analysis.treatment: Modifier on all tasks, per component. Uses trim-specific height tiers, not FAC_EXT_ACCESS.

scenarios.notes: Ground-level trim. No ladder needed. Baseline rate.
Extension ladder required. Slower production due to reach and stability.
Long extension ladder or scaffold. Safety overhead significant. Rest breaks at height.
Scaffold or lift mandatory. Extreme height premium. May require 2-person crew for safety.

exterior_height_analysis.repaint_note: Height modifier is especially impactful on trim repaint because trim prep at height (scraping, feather sanding) requires stable positioning and fine motor control that are compromised at elevation. Unlike siding where spray can be used from ground with extension, trim brush work at roofline requires the painter to be AT the working height.

exterior_complexity_analysis.treatment: Modifier on all tasks, per component type.

profiles.notes: Baseline. Single flat surface, no profile detail.
Single-piece with routed profile. Slightly more brush attention in profile grooves.
Multi-piece assembly. Multiple edges and joints to address. Caulking at assembly joints.

examples: window surround with pilasters and cap/sill
profiles.notes: Complex multi-piece with decorative elements. Significant brush time in detail areas. Historic homes and high-end residential.

key_decisions.topic: All-component scope — single spec covers all trim types
key_decisions.decision: Single spec covers fascia, rake, frieze, corner boards, band boards, window casings, door casings, and sills.
key_decisions.rationale: All exterior trim components share the same workflow (assess → prep → prime → coat), same substrate states, same quality tier range, and same modifier set. Splitting into per-component specs would create unnecessary fragmentation. The engine processes each component independently via its PS key — the spec structure handles multi-component routing.

key_decisions.decision: All trim components measured in LF. PCA P10 one-foot rule: trim <12 inches wide = 1 SF per 1 LF.
key_decisions.rationale: Exterior trim is predominantly narrow profile stock (1x4 through 1x12). LF is the natural measurement unit for linear components. The one-foot rule eliminates the need for width-based SF calculation on standard trim.

key_decisions.topic: QT3-QT5 range — trim is fine-finish substrate
key_decisions.decision: Quality tier range is QT3 through QT5. QT2 excluded.
key_decisions.rationale: Trim IS a fine-finish substrate — sheens are satin (QT3), semi-gloss (QT4), or gloss (QT5). Trim is viewed at close range and is a detail surface. Economy prep (QT2) produces unacceptable results on trim. QT5 is appropriate for trim (unlike siding where QT5 is excluded).

key_decisions.decision: Include SC_SOUND through SC_SEVERE_DETERIORATION (DSD 0-3). SC_SUBSTRATE_DAMAGE (DSD-4) = hard stop.
key_decisions.rationale: DSD-equivalent condition rating drives the prep labor multiplier (1.0x to 1.75x). This is the dominant COST driver for repaint estimation alongside substrate state. DSD-4 = structural damage (rot) which is outside painting scope.

key_decisions.topic: Substrate material as modifier, not dimension
key_decisions.decision: Substrate material (wood/PVC/engineered) is a MODIFIER, not a configuration dimension.
key_decisions.rationale: Substrate material affects primer selection only — the overall workflow structure (assess → prep → prime → coat) does not change. Making it a full dimension would create unnecessary variant explosion (4 states x 4 conditions x 3 tiers x 3 materials = 144 variants vs 48 without material). Primer selection lookup handles material as a modifier.

key_decisions.decision: Use FAC_TRRP_HEIGHT with trim-specific tiers (1.00/1.30/1.60/1.90/2.20), not FAC_EXT_ACCESS.
key_decisions.rationale: Trim height tiers (1.30/1.60/1.90/2.20) differ from siding access tiers (1.35/1.60/1.50). Trim requires the painter to be AT working height for brush work — no ground-level spray with extension. Per-component assignment (fascia = high tier, ground-level casings = baseline).

Profile complexity significantly affects both prep and coating production rates. Simple flat board vs elaborate 3-piece crown is a 1.60x difference. Per-component assignment — one building may have simple and elaborate trim.

key_decisions.topic: Caulking integrated — not a separate spec
key_decisions.decision: Caulk assessment and replacement is an integral part of the trim repaint workflow.
key_decisions.rationale: Caulk failure at trim joints is the #1 cause of premature trim coating failure. Every trim repaint includes caulk assessment — it cannot be scoped separately without leaving gaps in waterproofing. SF_CAULK_EXT_v1 is for standalone caulk-only jobs, not for caulking during a trim repaint.

key_decisions.decision: Brush is the primary (default) application method. Spray is conditional.
key_decisions.rationale: Trim brush rate (40 LF/hr) is often more productive than spray system rate (spray pass + masking = ~50-75 LF/hr) for small-to-medium trim volumes. Spray is only justified when full-house trim repaint provides sufficient volume to amortize masking overhead. Application method is a configuration dimension, not an assumption.

key_decisions.decision: RRP is a gate condition modifier on prep tasks, NOT a separate spec.
key_decisions.rationale: Pre-1978 building age triggers RRP for all paint disturbance. RRP adds containment, wet scraping, HEPA vacuum, and disposal overhead. Trim is HIGH RISK for lead paint — historically trim received oil-based lead paint more frequently than field surfaces. Creating a separate spec would fragment the estimation flow.

key_decisions.topic: Feather-edge sanding mandatory at all scraped areas
key_decisions.decision: Feather-edge sanding is MANDATORY whenever scraping occurs — non-negotiable at all quality tiers.
key_decisions.rationale: Every scraped edge on trim creates a visible ridge ('mapping') that telegraphs through topcoats. Trim is viewed at close range where mapping is most visible. Feather sanding is not a quality-tier-dependent upgrade — it is baseline practice.

key_decisions.decision: PVC trim requires LRV >=55 or solar-reflective coating technology.
key_decisions.rationale: Cellular PVC has high thermal expansion coefficient. Dark colors (LRV <55) cause thermal distortion — warping, buckling, joint opening. This is a material-specific gate condition checked during color approval, not during estimation. Flag only.

key_decisions.decision: Condition assessment is a REQUIRED fixed-time task before any prep or coating work.
key_decisions.rationale: Repaint trim cannot be estimated without inspecting existing surface condition. Assessment determines substrate state, DSD rating, rot locations, moisture content, and lead risk. This is a fundamental difference from NC.

key_decisions.decision: Rot repair is carpentry/contractor scope. Painting spec flags rot and excludes affected LF.
key_decisions.rationale: Painting over rot is cosmetic-only and fails within one season. Rot repair requires carpentry skills and materials outside the painting trade. After repair, new wood enters spec as SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD and receives full prep/prime treatment.

proposed_new_keys.rationale: Trim substrate material drives primer selection and material-specific constraints (PVC LRV check, engineered edge seal). Not needed for siding specs where material is implicit in the spec family (SF_SIDING_WOOD_*, SF_SIDING_FIBERCEMENT_*, etc.).
proposed_new_keys.notes: Project-level. Most residential projects have uniform trim material, but mixed material is possible (wood fascia with PVC corner boards).

proposed_new_keys.rationale: Per-component height tier for FAC_TRRP_HEIGHT modifier. Unlike siding where access_type is per-elevation, trim height is per-component — fascia may be at extreme tier while ground-level casings are baseline.
proposed_new_keys.notes: Set per trim component during scope capture. Multiple height tiers expected per project.

proposed_new_keys.rationale: Per-component profile complexity for FAC_TRRP_COMPLEXITY modifier. Complexity significantly affects production rates (1.0x to 1.60x).
proposed_new_keys.notes: Set per trim component type during scope capture. Mixed complexity common — simple corner boards with elaborate window surrounds.

proposed_new_keys.rationale: Triggers EPA Lead-Safe RRP requirements for all prep tasks involving paint disturbance. Building age is the gate — if pre-1978, RRP applies unless lead testing proves absence.
proposed_new_keys.notes: Project-level flag. Shared with siding RP and all repaint exterior specs.

proposed_new_keys.rationale: Siding area adjacent to trim requiring masking when trim is sprayed. Measured as LF of trim-siding junction x standard mask width (12-24 inches).
proposed_new_keys.notes: Only needed when application_method = spray. Not applicable for brush trim work.

research_corrections.original_claim: Notion prompt says 'substrate_condition' as config dimension — need to clarify this is DSD-equivalent for trim
research_corrections.corrected_to: Substrate condition for trim uses the same DSD-equivalent scale as wood siding RP: SC_SOUND through SC_SEVERE_DETERIORATION. Condition modifier applies to prep tasks only, stacking multiplicatively with height modifier. Same partitioning as wood siding RP.
research_corrections.corrected_by: Spec Researcher Agent (per user brief RC-001)

research_corrections.original_claim: Trim height modifier values (1.30/1.60/1.90/2.20) differ from siding access modifier (1.35/1.60/1.50)
research_corrections.corrected_to: Trim uses its own height tiers via FAC_TRRP_HEIGHT (1.00/1.30/1.60/1.90/2.20), NOT FAC_EXT_ACCESS (1.00/1.35/1.60/1.50). Trim height is per-component (fascia at roofline vs casing at ground level), while siding access is per-elevation. The modifier values are different because trim work requires the painter to be AT working height for brush work — no ground-level spray with extension.
research_corrections.corrected_by: Spec Researcher Agent (per user brief RC-002)

research_corrections.original_claim: Doctrine says spray rate 200 SF/hr 'including masking' for trim
research_corrections.corrected_to: 200 SF/hr is a SYSTEM rate combining spray pass + masking overhead. This is NOT a task rate. The spray task rate for trim is 100-150 LF/hr (spray pass only). Masking is a SEPARATE task at 30-50 LF/hr. System rate is for planning/comparison purposes only — individual tasks need individual rates.
research_corrections.corrected_by: Spec Researcher Agent (per user brief RC-003)

research_corrections.original_claim: Environmental conditions should affect trim estimation
research_corrections.corrected_to: Environmental conditions (wind, dew point, sun exposure, surface temperature) are EXCLUDED from estimation modifiers. They are unpredictable at bid time and belong in SOP/process documentation. Per established exterior spec convention.
research_corrections.corrected_by: Spec Researcher Agent (per established doctrine pattern)

doctrine_gaps: Trim-specific production rate calibration — doctrine rates for 40 LF/hr brush are averages across all trim types. Per-component rates (fascia vs casing vs sill) may differ and need field validation.
DSD multiplier precision within bands — doctrine provides ranges (e.g., 1.25-1.5x for DSD-2) but not exact values. Using midpoints as defaults pending field calibration.
RRP labor premium on trim — estimated 1.40x but trim prep at height with RRP containment may be higher than siding RRP premium due to awkward positioning.

Mixed substrate material handling — how to estimate a project with wood fascia and PVC corner boards. Currently handled as per-component modifier but no doctrine guidance on project-level optimization.
field_calibration_needed: Per-component brush production rates (fascia LF/hr vs window casing LF/hr vs sill LF/hr)
Complexity modifier validation (1.00 / 1.15 / 1.30 / 1.60 bands — derived from doctrine '30-60%' range)
Height modifier impact on trim scraping (scraping at 17-19 ft is estimated at 1.90x but may be higher due to fine motor demands)
Caulk replacement rate for old caulk removal (50-100 LF/hr range is wide — depends on old sealant type and age)
Spray break-even point — at what total trim LF does spray become more productive than brush (considering masking overhead)?
RRP containment at height — setup/teardown times for poly containment on ladders and scaffolds

Condition assessment for trim components (DSD rating, adhesion testing, moisture content, coating ID, rot probe)
Primer selection and application based on substrate state AND substrate material (spot prime, chalk-binding, full prime)
Finish coat application on all 8 trim component types
Caulk assessment and replacement at trim-to-adjacent-surface joints (trim side)
Lead paint evaluation and RRP compliance when pre-1978 (containment, wet methods, disposal)
Ground-level protection from scraping debris and paint drips
Siding masking when trim is sprayed (siding protection FROM trim spray overspray)
Window/door masking when painting adjacent casings

Soffit/porch ceiling painting — owned by soffit spec
Window painting (frame, sash, muntins) — owned by window ext RP spec
Door painting (slab face, frame) — owned by door ext RP spec
Foundation wall painting — owned by foundation spec

Scaffold setup/teardown — shared resource, allocated by project

assumptions.value: Repaint of existing exterior trim — all components (fascia, rake, frieze, corner, band, window casing, door casing, sill). Condition-dependent prep and coating.
assumptions.note: Siding, windows, doors, soffit are separate specs. Rot repair is carpentry scope.

assumptions.value: SS_EXT_WEATHERED excluded from trim substrate states
assumptions.note: Trim that has lost all coating and weathered is effectively bare wood — enters scope via rot repair as SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD. Weathered trim without coating is a maintenance failure that indicates prior neglect, and the structural integrity must be assessed before painting.

assumptions.value: SS_EXT_STAINED_SOLID and SS_EXT_STAINED_SEMI excluded from this spec
assumptions.note: Stained trim recoating is a separate scope with unique material and compatibility requirements.

assumptions.value: QT2 not applicable to exterior trim
assumptions.note: Trim is a fine-finish substrate viewed at close range. Economy prep produces unacceptable results. QT3 is the minimum acceptable tier.

assumptions.value: SC_SUBSTRATE_DAMAGE (DSD-4) is outside painting scope — hard stop requiring structural repair
assumptions.note: DSD-4 indicates rot, structural compromise. Cannot be addressed by painting — requires carpentry scope.

assumptions.value: Lead-safe RRP is a modifier on prep tasks, not a separate spec. Triggered by building year (pre-1978).
assumptions.note: RRP adds containment, wet methods, HEPA vacuum, and disposal overhead. Estimated 1.40x labor premium on affected prep tasks. Trim is high-risk for lead paint.

assumptions.value: Brush is the primary (default) application method for exterior trim repaint
assumptions.note: Spray conditional on sufficient volume to justify masking overhead. Break-even point estimated at ~500 LF total trim.

uncertainties.detail: Doctrine provides a single 40 LF/hr baseline for exterior trim brush work. Actual rates likely vary by component: fascia (accessible, long runs) may be faster than window casing (complex profile, interruptions) or sill (horizontal, catches debris). No per-component rate data in doctrine.
uncertainties.recommendation: Field calibration with timed brush work per trim component type. Start with 40 LF/hr baseline for all components and adjust after field data collection.

uncertainties.detail: Doctrine provides multiplier ranges per DSD level (e.g., 1.25-1.5x for DSD-2) but not exact values. Using midpoints as defaults (1.15 for DSD-1, 1.375 for DSD-2, 1.75 for DSD-3).
uncertainties.recommendation: Field calibration with timed prep data across DSD levels to narrow midpoint values.

uncertainties.detail: At what total trim LF does spray application become more productive than brush, considering masking overhead? Estimated ~500 LF but not validated. Below break-even, brush is faster because no masking time.
uncertainties.recommendation: Compare total project time (brush-only vs spray+mask) at various trim LF totals (200, 500, 1000, 2000 LF) through estimation runs.

uncertainties.topic: Mixed substrate material on same building
uncertainties.detail: A single building may have wood fascia, PVC corner boards, and engineered band board. The per-component modifier approach handles this, but project-level material procurement and primer inventory becomes complex.
uncertainties.recommendation: Document per-component material assignment in PaintScope input. Materials manager handles multi-material primer procurement.

uncertainties.detail: RRP containment setup/teardown at elevation (scaffold/ladder) is significantly more complex than at ground level. The 1.40x RRP multiplier may understate the overhead for high-elevation trim scraping with containment.
uncertainties.recommendation: Field calibration of RRP setup/teardown times at different height tiers. May need height-adjusted RRP multiplier (1.40x at ground, 1.60x at height).

uncertainties.detail: Caulk LF is derived from component count and typical joint frequency, but actual joint count varies significantly by building design. Victorian-era homes may have 5x the caulk joints of a modern ranch.
uncertainties.recommendation: Use default derivation rules for initial estimate. Allow estimator override based on site assessment.
